research_question: Compare photocatalytic dye degradation performance under matched task, metric, units, material, pollutant, and budget.

documents.title: Visible-light degradation of methylene blue over TiO2-N (Synthetic Example)

paragraphs.text: Task: photocatalytic degradation. Material: N-doped TiO2. Pollutant: methylene blue. Metric: removal efficiency. Units: %. Budget: 0.5 g/L catalyst for 60 min under 300 W Xe lamp.

Methods: Absorbance at 664 nm was grouped by triplicate reaction batches (n=3), normalized to dark-equilibrated baseline C0, filtered for steady-state drift < 5%, yielding percentage removal efficiency. Main conclusion: N-doped TiO2 achieved 91.2% removal, outperforming bare TiO2 baseline (54.0%). Limitation: long-term reuse beyond 3 cycles was not tested.

documents.title: Photocatalytic removal of rhodamine B over N-doped TiO2 (Synthetic Example)

paragraphs.text: Task: photocatalytic degradation. Material: N-doped TiO2. Pollutant: rhodamine B. Metric: removal efficiency. Units: %. Budget: 0.5 g/L catalyst for 60 min under 300 W Xe lamp.
Main conclusion: N-doped TiO2 achieved 62.5% removal of rhodamine B (n=3), lower than reported methylene blue benchmarks due to differing dye structure.
